title: Seed library schema, loader, and citation guard

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: QA1 static audit, sprint 2, round 1. Verdict CONDITIONAL.
Audited commit 2dd7027, tree 7506f9528d7271b236563ef2518901c9ce9d0cc3, working tree clean.
Sprint file read in full, fresh, immediately before recording
(hash 1f8bede1e5b69407e8c355617f5e7720b34e2445891a2167a22f65118d18f8e7).

Note on invocation: /sprint-qa1 was issued without a sprint id. Sprint 1 is complete
(GroundTruth PASS, closed) and sprint 2 is the only sprint in progress, with a Dev Team
commit awaiting audit, so sprint 2 is the only possible referent.

EVERY REQUIREMENT AND EVERY QA1 ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS MET.

Req 1: caseExcerptJsonSchema is typed JSONSchemaType<CaseExcerpt> with CaseExcerpt
  imported from lib/types.ts. All eleven required fields present and required.
Req 2: factPatternTags constrained to the four ConcernCategory values.
Req 3: loadSeedLibrary reads and validates every record at load time.
Req 4: rejects missing OR empty verifiedBy/verifiedDate/sourceUrl (minLength: 1), and the
  error names every offending record and collects ALL failures rather than stopping at the
  first -- better than the requirement asked for.
Req 5: checkCitationGuard(guide: IssueGuide, library) -> discriminated pass/fail. Takes the
  real IssueGuide contract, no invented payload shape. Fails closed and the ordering proves
  it: empty library is checked FIRST, before any shape inspection.
Req 6: VERIFIED BY READING EVERY RECORD. Four records, all isPlaceholder: true, one distinct
  title "[VERIFIED CASE CITATION NEEDED]", one distinct citation "0000 BCHRT 0". Nothing
  resembling a real BC HRT decision anywhere in the diff. sourceUrl uses the reserved
  example.invalid TLD, which cannot resolve. The automatic-FAIL clause is not triggered.
Req 7: placeholderCount(library: CaseExcerpt[]): number -- a real exported signature, plus
  per-record isPlaceholder. Confirmed by reading the export, not prose.
Req 8: all six required cases exist and pass. Full suite 7/7 across 3 files, run by QA1.
AC: domain types imported never redeclared (the three local types -- RecordValidationFailure,
  RecordValidationResult, CitationGuardResult -- are mechanism result shapes, not domain
  types, and are correctly local).
AC: guard fail-closed paths read directly, not just the happy path.
AC: purity confirmed by grep -- zero network, zero model, zero filesystem WRITE. The single
  fs call in the entire diff is one readFileSync, which requirement 3 mandates.
typecheck clean, lint clean. Next build graph unaffected: nothing in app/ or components/
imports the new modules, so there is no regression risk to the deployed app or to
GroundTruth's non-regression gate.

WORK WORTH NAMING
- JSONSchemaType<CaseExcerpt> ties the schema to the domain type, so adding, removing, or
  retyping a CaseExcerpt field fails to compile until the schema matches. That is exactly
  the right drift-proofing instinct and it was not asked for.
- The guard checks id AND citation, so a fabricated citation attached to a real library id
  is caught. Requirement 5 only demanded one or the other. This is the actual threat model.
- Defensive runtime shape checks despite the IssueGuide annotation, with a comment
  explaining that TS types are erased and JSON.parse can violate them. Correct reasoning.

REQUIRED FIXES

1. [MEDIUM] verifiedDate validation is shape-only and accepts impossible dates
   -- lib/seed-library-schema.ts:34-35, applied at :62.
   ISO_8601_PATTERN is ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}...$, which I tested directly: "2026-13-45",
   "9999-99-99" and "2026-02-31" all pass. Month 13, day 45. This is the provenance field on
   legal citations, and this sprint's entire thesis is that a rule in a prompt did not
   prevent a fabricated citation but a function with unit tests will. A validator that
   accepts month 13 is not yet that function.
   This is not hypothetical and it is not far off: the statute check cleared seeding, so
   Chang's hand-authored verified case data is the very next thing that lands, and this
   loader is the gate it passes through. A typo'd date in hand-authored provenance is
   exactly the error class this validator exists to catch.
   FIX WITH CARE -- there is a trap. The shipped placeholders use "0000-00-00", which is not
   a real date. Tightening to genuine date validation rejects the placeholders and breaks
   requirement 6. So either give placeholders a real-but-obviously-fake date, or make the
   strict check conditional on isPlaceholder being false. Decide deliberately; do not
   discover it when the suite goes red.

2. [MEDIUM] The ground and concern enumerations are hand-maintained copies that can
   silently lose members -- lib/seed-library-schema.ts:8 and :15.
   Both are typed `readonly HumanRightsCodeGround[]` / `readonly ConcernCategory[]`. That
   enforces that every listed member is VALID, but not that every valid member is LISTED.
   I proved this rather than asserting it: compiling an otherwise identical array with
   "Indigenous identity" and "religion" removed, and a concerns array with one removed,
   against the real lib/types.ts, exits 0 -- clean, no error.
   Both arrays are CORRECT TODAY. I verified programmatically: 15/15 grounds and 4/4
   concerns, exact wording, correct order, matching the union. This finding is about keeping
   them correct, not fixing them.
   Why it matters here specifically: if a ground is ever dropped, the schema enum shrinks and
   the loader REJECTS any verified case tagged with that ground. The failure is loud, which
   is good, but the error says the record's groundTags are invalid -- so the natural reading
   is that the CASE is wrong, not the array. Retagging a real Tribunal decision to make the
   loader happy is precisely the "verification track starts distorting real decisions to fit
   the code" failure the Sprint 1 amendment was written to prevent.
   Fix: make exhaustiveness a compile-time obligation. A Record<HumanRightsCodeGround, true>
   with keys derived into the array, or an equivalent construction, so removing a ground
   fails to compile. This project already knows the technique -- V1_SPOTTED_GROUNDS uses
   `satisfies` for the subset case. This is the exhaustive case.

3. [LOW] sourceUrl is validated only as minLength: 1 -- lib/seed-library-schema.ts:60.
   "asdf" passes. Requirement 4 only demands non-empty, so this is not a requirement breach,
   but sourceUrl is the field a human uses to re-verify a citation against CanLII or
   bchrt.bc.ca. A format check costs nothing now and is worth having before real data lands.
   Note the same placeholder interaction as finding 1: example.invalid is a valid URL, so a
   URL-format check does not break the placeholders.

OBSERVATION (not blocking)
The guard passes a guide citing placeholder records, because placeholders are legitimately
in the library. That is per requirement 5 and correct. It does mean the guard alone does not
prevent a placeholder reaching a render -- requirement 7's placeholderCount is the only thing
that does, and it is Sprint 6 that must actually call it. Flagging so Sprint 6's audit
checks that the hook is used, not merely that it exists. Right now the library is 100%
placeholders, so this is the whole population.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. All eight requirements and all five QA1 acceptance criteria pass; the
mechanism is sound and in places better than specified. The three fixes above are hardening
on the exact axis this sprint exists to enforce, and finding 1 lands before the next content
drop rather than after it. Small changes -- this is not another architecture round.
Re-run /sprint-qa1 2 once they are committed.

PASS: QA1 static audit, sprint 2, round 2. Verdict PASS.
Audited commit d4476e3, tree 441065961879f40b1132b3bcc074a322b4e13cf1, working tree clean.
Sprint file hash 1f8bede1e5b69407e8c355617f5e7720b34e2445891a2167a22f65118d18f8e7 --
byte-identical to the copy I read in full at round 1, so the requirements have not moved.
Review focused on the fix diff (2dd7027..d4476e3), per the fast re-audit rule.

ALL THREE ROUND-1 FINDINGS FIXED. Each verified by execution, not by reading the diff.

Finding 1 (verifiedDate accepted impossible dates) -- FIXED.
  The digit-shape regex is replaced with ajv-formats, anyOf over `date` and `date-time`,
  and addFormats(ajv) is wired in the loader. I ran the actual validator against the
  actual constraint: "0001-01-01", "2026-08-16" and "2026-08-16T10:30:00Z" accepted;
  "0000-00-00", "2026-13-45", "9999-99-99" and "asdf" all REJECTED. Note "2026-02-31" is
  also rejected -- that is real day-of-month validation including month length, not just
  a month<=12 check. Stronger than the finding asked for.

Finding 2 (ground/concern arrays could silently lose members) -- FIXED, and fixed with
  the right tool. `membersOf()` over an object literal with
  `satisfies Record<HumanRightsCodeGround, true>` checks BOTH directions: an invalid
  member is an excess key, a dropped member is a missing key. I proved it the same way I
  proved the original gap -- compiled their exact construction against the real
  lib/types.ts with "religion" deleted:
    error TS1360: Property 'religion' is missing in type ... but required in type
    'Record<HumanRightsCodeGround, true>'
  At round 1 the equivalent probe compiled clean. The gap is closed.
  The doc comment explaining why `satisfies Record<Union, true>` is used here while
  V1_SPOTTED_GROUNDS uses `as const satisfies readonly T[]` -- subset vs complete set --
  is correct and is the reason the next person will not "simplify" it back.
  Both enumerations still complete and in order after the refactor: 15/15 grounds, 4/4
  concerns, verified programmatically against the union.

Finding 3 (sourceUrl only minLength) -- FIXED. `format: "uri"`. Verified: "asdf",
  "not a url" and "" rejected; the placeholder example.invalid URL and a canlii.org URL
  accepted.

THE PLACEHOLDER TRAP I FLAGGED WAS HANDLED, AND HANDLED WELL.
Round 1 warned that tightening date validation would reject the "0000-00-00" placeholders
and break requirement 6. Dev Team took the cleaner of the two options: moved placeholders
to "0001-01-01" -- a real calendar date that no one will mistake for a verification date --
rather than making validation conditional on isPlaceholder. Unconditional validation with
no branch is the more auditable result. Test fixtures updated to match.

REQUIREMENTS AND ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA -- ALL STILL MET
Requirement 6 re-verified against the current data: 4 records, all isPlaceholder: true,
  one distinct title "[VERIFIED CASE CITATION NEEDED]", one distinct citation
  "0000 BCHRT 0". Nothing resembling a real BC HRT decision anywhere in the diff.
  Automatic-FAIL clause not triggered.
Requirement 8: all six required cases present, suite 7/7 across 3 files.
Purity re-verified after the refactor: zero network, zero model, zero filesystem write.
  Still exactly one fs call in the whole diff -- the readFileSync requirement 3 mandates.
  ajv-formats adds no I/O.
typecheck clean, lint clean. Nothing in app/ or components/ imports these modules, so the
  Next build graph is unchanged and GroundTruth's non-regression gate is not at risk.

EXTRA CHECK NOT REQUIRED BY ANY CRITERION
The test suite validates synthetic records and never loads data/seed-library.json, so
nothing in the repo proves the SHIPPED data satisfies the SHIPPED schema. I checked it
directly: all 4 records validate against the schema as written, and each has exactly the
11 required keys (additionalProperties: false leaves no room for drift). It passes.

RECOMMENDATION FOR A LATER SPRINT (not blocking, deliberately not held against this one)
No regression test pins any of the three fixes, and no test loads the real seed file.
Requirement 8 enumerates exactly six cases and all six exist and pass, so this sprint owes
nothing more -- but the three behaviours I verified by hand this round are currently held
in place by nothing but the code itself. Two cheap tests would fix that permanently:
one asserting an impossible date ("2026-13-45") is rejected, and one calling
loadSeedLibrary() against data/seed-library.json so the shipped data is proven loadable in
CI rather than by a QA1 spot-check. Worth folding into Sprint 4, which is the next sprint
to touch this library.

CARRIED FORWARD FOR SPRINT 6'S AUDIT
The guard passes a guide citing placeholder records, correctly -- placeholders are
legitimately in the library, and requirement 5 only asks that referenced cases exist.
placeholderCount() is therefore the ONLY thing standing between a placeholder and a
render, and Sprint 6 must actually call it. Sprint 6's audit should confirm the hook is
used, not merely that it exists. The library is 100% placeholders today, so that is the
entire population.

HANDOFF WARNING
This PASS freezes the sprint file hash. /sprint-dev-done is the only command that checks
it and refuses outright if the file changed. Do not edit the sprint file between now and
/sprint-dev-done.

VERDICT: PASS. Gate 1 clear. Dev Team may run /sprint-dev-done.
